what:
User-directed design decisions for hook visibility fast-follow (Apr 22 2026, refines mems #175, #307, #310):

**Visibility philosophy (user-specified):**
- Don't duplicate what Claude Code already shows (MCP tool responses, tool call chrome, already-visible labels)
- Surface what's otherwise invisible (silent additionalContext injections, correction detection, session-start memory injection)
- Goal: users understand what aide-memory is doing without noise

**Reason text on emitBlockDecision stays UNCHANGED:**
- Reason is shown to Claude AND the user. Claude acts on the reason text — changing it affects agent behavior.
- User-facing reframing goes in `systemMessage`, which is user-only. Not redundant because systemMessage is reassurance not instruction.
- Prior analysis that Option 2 was "redundant" was wrong — it conflated Claude-facing vs user-facing channels.

**Fast-follow ship list (finalized):**
| Hook | Change |
|---|---|
| pre-read-recall (soft) | + systemMessage "aide-memory · N memories recalled for {path}" |
| pre-read-recall (hard block) | + systemMessage (user-only reassurance), reason unchanged |
| pre-edit-recall | same pattern as read |
| pre-search-nudge | + systemMessage "aide-memory · {term} has N memories — try aide_search" |
| detect-correction | + systemMessage "aide-memory · correction detected, saving as preference ({scope})" |
| session-start-clear | + systemMessage "aide-memory · N memories injected (layers: ...)" if injected |
| stop-remember | no change — already soft, reason fine |
| pre-compact-save | no change — cleanup only, not meaningful to surface |
| track-* (Pre/PostToolUse on MCP) | no change — already visible via tool response |

**Wording for hard-block systemMessage (draft):**
- `aide-memory · scoped memories found — prompting recall before read`
(user reassurance, doesn't duplicate reason's instruction, active voice, no "error"/"crash" words)

**Config:**
- Single global `hooks.output.visible` (default on)
- Consolidate dangling `nudge.visible` in src/memory/config.ts

**Option G (auto-inject) → separate spec:**
- Write `docs/specs/PHASE_1_FOLLOWUP_AUTO_INJECT_RECALL.md` as its own spec file
- Reference from `PHASE_0_1_SPEC.md` / `PHASE_0_1_VALIDATION_FOLLOWUPS.md` under fast-follows
- No code changes until user greenlights
- Design: `recall.mode: "agent" | "autoInject"`, default "agent"

**PreToolUse "blocking error" label:**
- Hardcoded in Claude Code, cannot fix. File Anthropic FR but don't block on it.

**Accepted error (future-session warning):** I fabricated "2 remember opportunities detected" for pre-compact-save without verifying handlers.ts — the hook is actually cleanup-only. Always read the handler code before writing per-hook design proposals. Lesson: verification before spec.
why: Important corrections from the user this turn: (1) reason text must stay unchanged (Claude-facing), systemMessage is for user-only reframing — not redundant; (2) don't duplicate Claude Code's native rendering; (3) Option G spec as its own file referenced from phase 0-1 doc; (4) pre-compact is cleanup only, not detection (I'd fabricated the prior description). These decisions bind the implementation and prevent the next session from reverting to the incorrect prior state. Also captures the methodological lesson about reading handler code before writing specs.
